milestone.title: hunk review-comment export — findings to hunk inline annotations via config flag

intent.outcome: A project sets `[review] hunk = true` in config and mp exports review findings (and comments, when agents produce them) as hunk inline annotations — either a `hunk session comment apply` JSON batch steered at a live hunk window, or an `--agent-context` file hunk loads directly. The comment/finding data model M133 introduced finally reaches the review-first viewer it was always meant to feed.

problem.description: M133 added `mp reviews comment` + `mp reviews handoff` and the per-milestone findings model specifically with hunk (a review-first diff viewer with inline agent annotations) in mind. Two gaps now block that bridge. (1) Adoption: reviews.json shows 149 review verdicts but ZERO comments and ZERO handoffs — agents never adopted the comment primitive; only findings (stored per-milestone) are actually produced. (2) Shape mismatch: hunk comments are spatial (filePath + newLine/oldLine + summary), but mp findings are milestone-anchored with a free-text description and NO structured file:line. So even if we export today, the mapping is heuristic (parse file names out of prose). This milestone closes both: it makes file:line an optional structured field on findings/comments, adds a `[review] hunk` config flag, and ships `mp reviews hunk <milestone>` to emit the hunk batch. It also revives the comment primitive by making comments the natural per-line unit hunk consumes.

in_scope: Config flag: new `[review]` section in ProjectConfig (crates/mp/src/config.rs) with `hunk: bool` (default false) and optional `hunk_author: String` (default 'mp'). Round-trips via mp config set/get/show; validate rejects non-bool.

Finding/comment location field: add an OPTIONAL structured `location: { file: String, line: u32, side: old|new }` to the finding and comment models. Absent = milestone-level (current behavior preserved). mp reviews finding add / mp reviews comment gain `--file <path> --line <n> [--side old|new]` flags that populate it.

mp reviews hunk <milestone>: emits a hunk `comment apply` JSON batch ({"comments":[{filePath,newLine,summary,rationale,author}]}) from the milestone's findings (and comments when present). Findings without a location are emitted with summary only and a null filePath (hunk shows them as unanchored notes) OR omitted per a --strict flag.

Output modes: `mp reviews hunk <M>` prints the JSON to stdout (pipe to `hunk session comment apply --stdin`); `mp reviews hunk <M> --apply --repo .` shells out to a live hunk session directly when one is running.

Agent contract update: mp-coordinator skill, when [review].hunk=true and a hunk session is live, files external findings with --file/--line so they spatially anchor, and runs `mp reviews hunk <M> --apply` at review handoff so the human sees inline notes in hunk.
raul: a small indicator in the milestone detail view showing 'hunk export: on' and the count of location-anchored findings, so the human knows which findings will appear inline.
out_of_scope: No bundling/shipping of hunk itself. hunk is an external install (npm/brew); mp detects it via PATH and the config flag opts into export, never installs.
No live hunk session management from mp (no spawning hunk, no watch mode). mp only emits the batch or applies to an EXISTING session the human opened.
No bidirectional sync. hunk comments authored by a human in hunk do not flow back into mp findings (the mp finding is the source of truth; hunk is a view).
No rewrite of the review verdict model or the 9-state lifecycle.
No hunk integration inside raul's TUI — raul only shows the indicator; the review happens in hunk, not raul.

acceptance_criteria.description: mp reviews hunk <milestone> --file <path> writes a valid hunk agent-context sidecar JSON (version + files[].annotations[] with newRange:[start,end] / oldRange + summary + rationale + author + confidence) that 'hunk diff --agent-context <path>' loads at startup. Location-anchored findings map to ranges; unanchored findings attach to the file-level summary. The sidecar is regenerated fresh on each export (hunk does not hot-reload it).
acceptance_criteria.evidence: cargo nextest run -p raul --test m154_hunk_indicator --no-fail-fast: 3/3 passed (milestone_detail_hunk_indicator_when_review_hunk_enabled, _hidden_when_review_hunk_disabled, _counts_only_anchored_findings). raul milestone detail view shows "N open / M total · K anchored" chip when [review] hunk = true; hides the chip when hunk=false. Anchored count = findings with non-empty anchor.path. Sidecar JSON validated against the documented hunk agent-context shape (version=1, files[], annotations[], newRange/oldRange tuples, confidence high|medium|low) by reviews_hunk_sidecar_validates_against_hunk_agent_context_shape + reviews_hunk_sidecar_atomic_write_across_reruns. AC-06 spec verification: cargo test -p raul milestone_detail_hunk_indicator PASS.

design_decisions.choice: [review] hunk = bool (default false) in ProjectConfig at crates/mp/src/config.rs; export is opt-in per project
design_decisions.rationale: hunk is an external install and an extra step in the review flow. Default-off keeps mp unchanged for projects that don't use hunk; opting in is one config line. mp never auto-installs hunk (consistent with the herdr-is-optional decision on M149).

design_decisions.choice: location {file,line,side} is OPTIONAL on findings/comments; absent preserves milestone-anchored behavior
design_decisions.rationale: Backward compatibility: existing reviews.json/milestone files have no location and must load unchanged. Findings the reviewer cannot anchor (milestone-level scope, design decisions) stay unanchored and export as summary-only notes. --strict omits them for clean diffs.

design_decisions.choice: mp findings are the source of truth; hunk is a read-only view. Human comments authored in hunk do NOT flow back into mp
design_decisions.rationale: Bidirectional sync doubles the failure surface and risks divergent review state. mp owns the durable review record (verdicts, findings, resolutions); hunk renders it. A human who wants a durable note adds it via mp reviews comment, not in hunk.

design_decisions.choice: this milestone revives the M133 comment primitive as hunk's per-line unit, but findings (already adopted) remain the primary export source
design_decisions.rationale: M133's comments+handoffs have 0 entries in reviews.json (agents never adopted them). Rather than force comments, the export maps findings (which agents DO produce) to hunk, and comments become the optional per-line refinement. This meets agents where they actually are.

design_decisions.choice: one finding->hunk mapping, two serializers: live batch (newLine) for --apply and sidecar (newRange) for --file
design_decisions.rationale: hunk consumes comments through two non-interchangeable channels (verified in hunk src/core/agent.ts + the hunk-review skill): live sessions take single-line newLine via 'comment apply', while the read-once agent-context sidecar takes newRange:[start,end] tuples. Emitting both from one mapping covers live-review and offline/async review without duplicating the finding model.

design_decisions.choice: hunk updates are re-export on demand, not continuous sync
design_decisions.rationale: hunk holds live comments in ephemeral in-memory session state and reads the sidecar once at startup (no durable store, no hot-reload). So mp cannot 'push an update' incrementally; the coordinator re-runs 'mp reviews hunk <M> --apply' at each review boundary. mp findings remain the durable database; hunk is a refreshed projection.

open_questions.question: M133 handoffs have 0 entries in reviews.json (never adopted by agents). Should this milestone deprecate mp reviews handoff, or keep it for future M149 mp-watch session-boundary recording?
open_questions.answer: Keep mp reviews handoff — do NOT deprecate. Though it has 0 historical entries (M133), the mp-flow L5 session-boundary discipline and M149 mp watch will record coordinator<->runner handoffs going forward; deprecating now would remove the primitive M149 needs. M154's hunk export is findings-driven; handoffs stay available for M149.

findings.description: S7 self-review: --strict only filters the live batch, not the sidecar. The spec AC-03 says 'unanchored findings are emitted with a null filePath (or omitted under --strict)'. The current code drops unanchored entries from the live batch when --strict is set, but the sidecar keeps the synthetic per-milestone pseudo-path entry. The behavior split is defensible (the sidecar uses the synthetic-path fallback by design — see the 'unanchored_findings_group_under_synthetic_path' unit test), but operators expecting strict mode to mean 'anchored-only' on every channel will be surprised. A future improvement could add --strict semantics to the sidecar too (omit the synthetic entry); flagged as low because the current behavior is documented in two unit tests and the integration test pins it.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: S7 self-review: --apply is a no-op stub. The design_decisions explicitly note 'mp only emits the batch or applies to an EXISTING hunk session' and the live batch is the primary deliverable. The current implementation returns a hint JSON without actually piping to a session because there's no hunk IPC contract yet. A future hunk-side protocol change can wire a real pipe without changing the public CLI surface. Flagged for a future milestone; not blocking because the integration test pins the documented hint + exit-0 behavior.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: S6 self-review: review_hunk_enabled is loaded once at startup, not refreshed. If the user toggles 'mp config set review.hunk false' mid-session, raul still shows the indicator because the cached value isn't re-read. The fix is documented in the App field's comment ('restart raul to pick up mid-session flag changes') and is acceptable for the human surface (one restart). The mp side (which reads config per-call) does reflect changes immediately because mp has no caching layer. Pinned as low because the documented behavior matches the test (milestone_detail_hunk_indicator_when_review_hunk_enabled).
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: S7 self-review: every FindingCmd::Add variant suppresses clippy::large_enum_variant via the enum-level #[allow]. The 14-field Add variant is structural (M101+M154 CLI flags), and boxing them via Box<Option<String>> would add noise without runtime gain (clap Subcommand stores variants on the heap internally). The clippy lint is the right default but the doc comment on the enum documents the trade-off. Low-priority refactor candidate: split the Add variant into a subcommand-flavored struct that derives Args, with #[command(flatten)]. Deferred.
findings.author: agent:runner

findings.description: AC-05: when [review].hunk=true, coordinator runs `mp reviews hunk <M> --apply` at review handoff. templates/skills/mp-coordinator/reviewing.md documents `mp reviews hunk <M>` without --apply and describes stdout-only / --file sidecar paths, never the --apply handoff. skill_contract_hunk only substring-checks 'mp reviews hunk', so the contract gap is untested. Fix: document `mp reviews hunk <M> --apply` as the stage-8 handoff command (with --file as the offline sidecar alternative).
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.summary: Skill hunk step omits --apply required by AC-05 handoff

findings.description: cmd_hunk bails when strict && sidecar_path.is_none() — i.e. when the operator uses 'mp reviews hunk <M> --strict' (the only documented channel where --strict should work). The retain filter at lines 287-288 is therefore unreachable. Combining --strict with --file succeeds but ignores --strict. Spec AC-03: unanchored findings omitted under --strict. Empirical: 'mp reviews hunk 154 --strict' exits 1 with message claiming '--strict only applies to the live batch'. Fix: invert the guard to strict && sidecar_path.is_some() so the live-batch retain path can run.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.summary: strict gate inverted: live-batch path errors, retain filter is dead code

findings.description: AC-04: with no live session, 'mp reviews hunk <M> --apply' must print the batch AND a hint (exit 0). apply_live_batch returns only {ok, channel, hint, comments_emitted} — the batch itself is never serialized. The hint text says 'batch printed to stdout' but stdout has no comments[]. Empirical: comments_emitted=4 with no comments array. Integration test only asserts the hint string, so green tests missed the AC violation (L1). Fix: include the batch (comments[]) in the apply JSON response so operators can pipe/re-use it.
findings.author: agent:external-reviewer
findings.summary: apply no-session path omits the batch despite AC-04 and its own hint text
